summary: Evening thread panic in runtime causes cascading API 5xx surge for one tenant
description: Issue summary: Around 18:20 UTC we observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses for requests routed to the us-east serving pool for a single dedicated tenant (LexiSearch). Impact: Customer saw ~60% error rate on chat/streaming requests and ~30% on embedding uploads for 18:20-18:55 UTC. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated capacity pool pinned to customer. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mixed workload from LexiSearch that includes long-chat generation (>2k tokens) and bulk embedding upload concurrently. 2) Observe runtime worker thread crashes and subsequent 502/503 responses from API gateway. Logs & traces: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/dashboard/s/serve/tenant-us-east Lexi thread panic trace: logs-redwood://prod/us-east/runtime/worker-7/2026-03-10T18:22:31Z (see stack frames w/ tokenizer::segmenter::process). Slack thread: #support-lexisearch (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345/p164)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LexiSearch account to send a simultaneous streaming chat request (long prompt + function calls) and a bulk embedding upload of ~12k items.
2) Observe increased prefetch activity and repeated KV cache invalidations in serving-runtime logs.
3) Monitor API Gateway 5xx rate and runtime worker restarts during the burst.
comments: 2026-03-10 18:26 - Aisha Nair (Support): Customer reports heavy error rates, provided request IDs and sample payloads. Initial triage: spikes correlate to one tenant's traffic pattern.

2026-03-10 18:34 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Observed repeated SIGABRT from runtime worker process; thread panic originates in tokenizer segmentation code after recent runtime hotpatch. Opening internal incident channel #inc-runtime-panic.

2026-03-10 19:22 - Diego Martinez (SRE): After rollback, runtime worker restarts stabilized and API 5xx rate dropped to baseline for the customer. Leaving ticket open for follow-ups and root cause analysis.
investigation_notes: Memory and GPU driver checks: NVML logs show transient GPU driver reset coincident with worker SIGABRT; GPU memory usage not at peak but post-reset fragmentation observed.
Stack traces point to tokenizer::segmenter::process -> tokenize_utf8_sequence -> std::vector resize in patched tokenizer library (new behavior introduced in runtime-hotpatch).

Prefetch/KV cache behaviour: Long streaming sessions caused frequent KV writes; combined with bulk embeddings, this created lock contention on kvcache shards causing coroutine queue growth and increased thread concurrency in runtime worker.

Amplification path: runtime thread panic leads to worker process crash -> Kubernetes restarts worker -> API gateway keeps retrying connections which temporarily increases connection churn and accept queue backlog -> additional 5xx from api-gateway while runtime pool recovers.
Correlation: error spike window matches customer activity (confirmed by customer logs and request-ids). No similar signals for other tenants in the same pool.
root_cause: A recent runtime hotpatch updated the tokenizer library with an aggressive internal buffer resize which can trigger a stack corruption when combined with high concurrency on kvcache prefetch locks. The stack corruption produced thread-level panics and worker process SIGABRTs. Worker crash/restart churn amplified load at the API gateway (retries and accept queue saturation), producing the observed 5xx surge for the affected tenant.
resolution: 1) Rolled back the runtime hotpatch to the previous stable tokenizer build (deployment rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789). 2) Applied temporary per-tenant ingress throttle for LexiSearch to prevent immediate re-flood during restarts. 3) Increased api-gateway accept_queue and provisional connection backoff to smooth retry amplification. 4) Performed rolling restarts of affected runtime shards and monitored NVML/GPU health. Result: error rate returned to baseline by 19:22 UTC.
postmortem_plan: Schedule 72-hour postmortem doc with Runtime and SRE (owner: Elena Park).
Add unit/integration tests to catch tokenizer buffer resize under high-concurrency kvcache patterns.
Add a counter metric for tokenizer-exception-rate and alert when >0.1% for 5m in any tenant pool.
Improve per-tenant prewarm throttling policy to avoid single-tenant amplification on restarts.
Review the hotpatch rollout procedure: add a 1-hour low-traffic canary window when touching tokenizer/kernel codepaths.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-Task: Patch tokenizer library to guard against stack corruption (assignee: Elena Park).
SRE-Task: Create automatic mitigation runbook for thread-panics that scales api-gateway backoff and enforces per-tenant throttles (assignee: Diego Martinez).
DX-Task: Publish guidance for customers about safe bulk-embedding and long-stream concurrency limits for dedicated pools.
OBS-Task: Add dashboard panel for tokenization error traces and a dedicated alert.
resolution_notes: Rollback + throttles restored customer service quickly. Customer confirmed recovery and resumed operations with reduced concurrency while engineering prepares a patch. LexiSearch requested a 1:1 sync to understand timeline for a permanent fix.
